subject: Mathematics
source: National Curriculum (KS1 Year 2: place value to 100; addition and subtraction)

lessons.title: Tens and ones
objectives: Understand that a 2-digit number is made of tens and ones
Read and write numbers to 100 in numerals and words

keywords.def: groups of ten; the left digit in a 2-digit number
single units; the right digit in a 2-digit number
a single numeral from 0 to 9

starter: Say Bismillah. Count in ones from 17 to 25.

teach.heading: Bundles of ten
bullets: Tens are drawn as long rods.
Ones are drawn as small cubes.
teach.note: Use base ten rods and cubes on screen or physical straws bundled in tens. Ask how many ones are in one ten.

teach.heading: Reading 34
teach.note: Show 3 rods and 4 cubes. The position of a digit decides its value. Ask: is the 3 in 34 worth 3 or 30?

teach.heading: Numbers to 100
teach.note: Highlight multiples of ten. Misconception: writing 'seventy' as 700 or 7. Zero is a placeholder.

teach.heading: Words and numerals
teach.note: Practise reading words and writing numerals. Watch for teen and ty confusion: fourteen and forty.

practice: How many tens and ones are in 47?
independent: Write the number: 5 tens and 3 ones, 8 tens and 0 ones, 2 tens and 9 ones.
Write in numerals: forty-two, sixty-five, ninety.
exit: How many tens in 58? How many ones?
lessons.homework: Find five 2-digit numbers around your home and say how many tens and ones each has.
lessons.send: SEND: use physical straws or base ten. EAL: pair number words with numerals. Stretch: tens and ones in 3-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Partitioning 2-digit numbers
objectives: Partition a 2-digit number into tens and ones
Partition in more than one way

keywords.def: split a number into parts
the value of a digit because of where it is

teach.heading: Standard partition
teach.note: Show 4 rods and 7 cubes next to 40 + 7. Link the model to the sentence.

teach.heading: Missing parts
teach.note: Children find the missing tens or ones. Ask: how did you know?

teach.heading: Another way
teach.note: Show flexible partitioning by exchanging one ten for ten ones. This is key for subtraction later.

teach.heading: Compare partitions
teach.note: Use the balance picture. Ask children to explain why both give 47.

practice: Write 52 in a different way as 40 + __.
independent: Find two different ways to partition 56.
lessons.homework: Choose four 2-digit numbers and partition each in two different ways.
lessons.send: SEND: use place value counters and base ten. Stretch: partition into hundreds, tens and ones.

lessons.title: Comparing and ordering to 100
objectives: Compare 2-digit numbers using <, > and =
Order numbers to 100

keywords.def: bigger than
smaller than
arrange from smallest to largest or the other way

starter: What is 57 as tens and ones?

teach.heading: Compare the tens first
teach.note: Show with rods. The tens digit gives the main size. Ask children to say the sentence in words.

teach.heading: Same tens
teach.note: When the tens are equal, look at the ones. Common error: comparing digits in the wrong order.

teach.heading: Order numbers
teach.note: Sort by tens first, then ones if needed. Use number cards on screen.

teach.heading: Largest to smallest
teach.note: Contrast ascending and descending. Ask which word means smallest first.

independent: Write three numbers that are greater than 60 and less than 70.
lessons.homework: Write six 2-digit numbers on cards and put them in order from smallest to largest.
lessons.send: SEND: use rods to compare. Stretch: compare 3-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Counting in 2s, 3s, 5s and 10s
objectives: Count forwards and backwards in 2s, 5s and 10s
Count in 3s

keywords.def: a number in a counting sequence, such as 5, 10, 15
a list of numbers that follows a rule

teach.heading: Counting in 10s
teach.note: Chant together and use a hundred square on the screen. Ask what stays the same (the ones digit 0).

teach.heading: Counting in 5s
teach.note: Link to hands: 4 hands is 20. Ask what the next numbers are after 35.

teach.heading: Counting in 2s
teach.note: Use pairs of shoes outside the door. Introduce even numbers. Counting backwards from 20 in 2s is harder.

teach.heading: Counting in 3s
bullets: Use a number line to check.
teach.note: Show jumps on a number line to 30. This is new in Year 2. Expect more mistakes after 12.

lessons.homework: Count in 5s to 60 and in 2s to 30 to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND: use a hundred square and colour the multiples. Stretch: count in 4s and 25s.

lessons.title: Number lines to 100
objectives: Place numbers on a number line from 0 to 100
Estimate the position of a number

keywords.def: make a sensible guess close to the real answer
in the middle between two numbers

teach.heading: A 0 to 100 line
teach.note: Draw the line with tens marked. Ask where 50 is and why. Note that 0 to 100 line is not the same as 0 to 10 scaled up.

teach.heading: Find 37
bullets: Place it just before the middle.
teach.note: Show how to find a number between two marked tens. Teach: first the tens, then the ones.

teach.heading: Estimate
bullets: An estimate does not need to be exact.
teach.note: Show a number line with an arrow pointing between marks. Children say the number that the arrow is closest to.

teach.heading: Halfway numbers
teach.note: Use the idea of halfway to place and round. Ask: how did you work it out?

practice: Where is 70 on a 0 to 100 line?
What number is halfway between 40 and 60?
independent: Draw a number line 0 to 100 and mark 25, 50, 75.
An arrow points between 60 and 70, near 70. Name a number it could be.
Estimate: where is 91 on the number line?
exit: What number is halfway between 10 and 30?
lessons.homework: Draw a 0 to 100 number line with a ruler. Mark 10 numbers of your choice.
lessons.send: SEND: use a pre-marked line. Stretch: number lines 0 to 1000 with marks at hundreds.

lessons.title: Number bonds to 20
objectives: Recall pairs of numbers that make 20
Use bonds to 10 to find bonds to 20

keywords.def: two numbers that add to make a given total
the answer when numbers are added

teach.heading: Remember bonds to 10
teach.note: Quick-fire recap with fingers. These are the base for bonds to 20.

teach.heading: Bonds to 20 with tens
teach.note: Show a ten frame with 16 and 4 more. The ones digit follows the same bond as in 10.

teach.heading: The pattern
teach.note: Ask children to notice the pattern: the ones digits make 10.

teach.heading: Missing numbers
teach.note: Children use bonds and the number line. Check by adding.

independent: Write 5 pairs of numbers that make 20.
lessons.homework: Make flash cards for bonds to 20 and practise them with a family member.
lessons.send: SEND: use two ten frames. Stretch: bonds to 100 in tens.

lessons.title: Adding ones to a 2-digit number
objectives: Add a 1-digit number to a 2-digit number without crossing a ten
Use known number facts

keywords.def: combine to find the total
a fact we already remember, such as 3 + 4 = 7

starter: Count on in ones from 36 to 41.

teach.heading: Use a known fact
teach.note: Show with rods and cubes: 3 tens and 3 ones plus 4 ones. Only the ones change.

teach.heading: More examples
teach.note: Link to the facts 2 + 6, 1 + 7, 5 + 3. Children say the fact first.

teach.heading: When does it cross ten?
teach.note: Ask: what happens when the ones make 10 or more? Preview the next lesson.

teach.heading: On a number line
teach.note: Draw the jumps. Compare with the known fact 2 + 5 = 7.

independent: Write three sums of your own that do not cross a ten.
lessons.homework: Solve ten additions of the form 2-digit + 1-digit, with no crossing of tens.
lessons.send: SEND: use base ten. Stretch: add 3-digit and 1-digit without crossing.

lessons.title: Adding across the next ten
objectives: Add ones by making the next ten
Use bonds to bridge ten

keywords.def: go across a ten by splitting the number to add

starter: How many more to get from 38 to 40?

teach.heading: Make the next ten
teach.note: Show a number line from 37 to 40 to 42. Explain why we split the 5.

teach.heading: Finish the sum
teach.note: Write the steps. Ask: why did we choose to split 5 into 3 and 2?

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: Children identify the bond to the next ten (8 and 2), then the remaining 4.

teach.heading: Check with ten frames
teach.note: Use a ten frame picture to visualise making ten and the leftover. Connect to partitioning.

practice: What do you add to 69 to get to 70?
independent: Write a rule to explain how to add across a ten.
exit: Show how you made the next ten.
lessons.homework: Solve eight sums that cross a ten and show your bridging steps.
lessons.send: SEND: use ten frames. Stretch: add 2-digit numbers using bridging in tens.

lessons.title: Adding tens to a 2-digit number
objectives: Add a multiple of ten to a 2-digit number
Add two multiples of ten

keywords.def: a number in the 10 times table, like 30

teach.heading: Tens are like ones
teach.note: Use rods. Adding tens works like adding ones, but the answer is in tens.

teach.heading: Add tens to any number
teach.note: Show 3 tens and 4 ones, add 2 tens. Ask which digit changes.

teach.heading: Crossing 100
teach.note: Mention that going past 100 is fine. 10 tens is 100. Ask for 60 + 60 = 120.

teach.heading: Money link
teach.note: A real-life link. Be careful that the context is pence, not pounds.

independent: Write a sum with an answer of 87 using a multiple of ten.
lessons.homework: Practise adding multiples of ten using a hundred square, ten sums.
lessons.send: SEND: use rods; skip count in tens. Stretch: add multiples of 100.

lessons.title: Adding two 2-digit numbers
objectives: Add two 2-digit numbers by adding the tens and ones
Use a partitioning method

keywords.def: split into tens and ones
writing numbers one under the other, ones under ones

teach.heading: Add tens, add ones
teach.note: Show partitioning of both numbers. Add the tens then the ones, then recombine.

teach.heading: Using rods and cubes
teach.note: Use base ten or a picture. Ask children to explain what each group is.

teach.heading: Column method
bullets: Add the ones first, then the tens.
teach.note: Introduce the layout. Emphasise lining up ones under ones. Sort out misalignments.

teach.heading: Practise
teach.note: Children choose partitioning or columns. Review answers: 57, 69, 89.

independent: A shop has 35 red apples and 42 green apples. How many altogether?
Make up a 2-digit addition with the answer 79.
lessons.homework: Solve six 2-digit additions (with no crossing of ten in the ones) and check each with a different method.
lessons.send: SEND: use place value counters in a column grid. Stretch: add three 2-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Adding with exchange
objectives: Add two 2-digit numbers when the ones make 10 or more
Exchange ten ones for one ten

keywords.def: swap ten ones for one ten (or ten tens for one hundred)
move the new ten into the tens column

starter: How many ones make one ten?

teach.heading: More than ten ones
teach.note: Use place value counters. Ask: what can we do when we have 13 ones?

teach.heading: Exchange
bullets: Put the 1 ten in the tens column.
teach.note: Physically move ten cubes to make a rod. Show the 'carry' digit written under the tens.

teach.heading: Add the tens
teach.note: Show the full column method. Check the answer by estimating: 36 + 27 is about 40 + 30 = 70.

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: Children work through it with a partner. Common error: forgetting to add the carried ten.

exit: What do you do when the ones make more than 9?
lessons.homework: Solve six sums needing exchange and check each by estimating first.
lessons.send: SEND: physical exchange with base ten. Stretch: add 3-digit and 2-digit numbers with exchange.

lessons.title: Subtracting ones and tens
objectives: Subtract a 1-digit number or a multiple of ten from a 2-digit number
Use known facts

keywords.def: take away
the amount between two numbers

teach.heading: Subtract ones
teach.note: Use a known fact. Cross out cubes from the ones. The tens do not change when we do not cross a ten.

teach.heading: Subtract tens
teach.note: Use rods. Subtracting tens works like subtracting ones. The ones stay the same.

teach.heading: Counting back
teach.note: Draw hops back on a number line. Subtract 20 by hopping back two tens.

teach.heading: Cross a ten
teach.note: Preview bridging back through a ten: subtract the ones to get to the ten first. Practice more in the next lessons.

independent: Make up two subtractions with the answer 42.
lessons.homework: Solve eight subtractions of 1-digit or multiples of ten from 2-digit numbers.
lessons.send: SEND: use rods and cubes. Stretch: subtract 100 from 3-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Subtracting two 2-digit numbers
objectives: Subtract a 2-digit number from a 2-digit number without exchange
Use partitioning and columns

keywords.def: writing numbers under each other and subtracting ones then tens

teach.heading: Subtract the tens
teach.note: Use rods and cubes. Remove 3 rods then 5 cubes. Ask what is left.

teach.heading: Then the ones
teach.note: Teach the check with addition. The inverse is an important habit.

teach.heading: Column method
teach.note: Line up tens and ones. Always start at the ones. The bigger number goes on top.

teach.heading: More practice
teach.note: Children try each. Common error: subtracting the smaller digit from the larger regardless of position.

independent: A bag has 75 sweets. 32 are eaten. How many are left?
lessons.homework: Solve six subtractions with no exchange and check each with addition.
lessons.send: SEND: use base ten on a place value mat. Stretch: three-digit subtraction with no exchange.

lessons.title: Subtracting with exchange
objectives: Subtract 2-digit numbers when exchange is needed
Exchange one ten for ten ones

keywords.def: swap one ten for ten ones so you can subtract

starter: How many ones in one ten?

teach.heading: Not enough ones
teach.note: Show 5 rods and 2 cubes. Break one rod into ten cubes. Now there are 4 rods and 12 cubes.

teach.heading: Now subtract
teach.note: Work through the column method with the exchange shown by crossing out and rewriting. Check by 25 + 27 = 52.

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: Children work along and explain each step. Common mistake: forgetting to reduce the tens by one.

teach.heading: Check it
bullets: Add the answer to the number subtracted.
teach.note: Reinforce checking. Ask: why does this work? Because addition and subtraction are inverses.

independent: Write a subtraction that needs exchange and solve it.
exit: How do you know you need to exchange?
lessons.homework: Solve six subtractions needing exchange and check each one by addition.
lessons.send: SEND: use place value counters on a mat to exchange. Stretch: exchange with 3-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Inverse operations and missing numbers
objectives: Use addition and subtraction as inverse operations
Find missing numbers in 2-digit calculations

keywords.def: the operation that undoes another operation
a hidden number in a number sentence

teach.heading: Undoing
bullets: You are back where you started.
teach.note: Use a number line to show 20 + 5 = 25 and 25 - 5 = 20. Link to fact families.

teach.heading: Three numbers, four facts
teach.note: Extend fact families to 2-digit numbers. Point out the whole (59) in each sentence.

teach.heading: Missing numbers
teach.note: Use the inverse. Show how to find a missing part or a missing whole.

teach.heading: Subtraction blanks
teach.note: In 'whole - part = part' the missing part is found by subtracting again. Check by adding.

practice: Write the fact family for 20, 35 and 55.
independent: Write the four facts for 18, 36 and 54.
Use 46 + 28 = 74 to write a subtraction fact.
lessons.homework: Make six missing-number questions with their answers on a separate sheet.
lessons.send: SEND: use a bar model to show whole and parts. Stretch: missing numbers with 3-digit numbers.

lessons.title: Word problems and review
objectives: Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction word problems
Choose an efficient method

keywords.def: a problem that needs two calculations
a drawing of bars that shows how the numbers in a problem fit together

teach.heading: Read, draw, solve
teach.note: Model the process. Underline the question. Decide what is the whole and what are the parts.

teach.heading: One-step example
teach.note: Show the bar model for 48 and 27 making a whole. Write the answer with the unit: chairs.

teach.heading: Subtraction example
teach.note: Check by adding 35 + 29 = 64. Ask: does the answer make sense (less than 64)?

teach.heading: Two-step example
bullets: She gets 20 more, then gives away 15.
teach.note: Show the steps in order. Ask: what do we need to find first?

practice: There are 52 children in the playground. 18 go in. How many are still out?
A box has 37 pencils and another has 45. How many altogether?
Maryam reads 26 pages, then 38 pages. How many pages?
independent: A shop has 90 cartons of milk. It sells 45 and gets 30 more. How many now?
Ibrahim has 73p. He spends 28p. How much is left?
Write your own two-step problem and solve it.
exit: There are 68 dates. 29 are eaten. How many are left?
Which operation will you use and why?
lessons.homework: Write and solve two word problems about your day, one using + and one using -.
lessons.send: SEND: use a template bar model and a checklist. EAL: pre-teach vocabulary. Stretch: three-step problems.
